about: What the command line, setup --print, doctor, ping and the server print, in English. {name} and {command} come from product.json; the other {placeholders} are filled where the text is used. A list is printed one line per item.
help: {name} {version}: local agent-behaviour analytics, one process + one small database.
A page script on your site (rrweb replay + clicks/typing + environment signals) sends visits to {name}'s own
collect endpoint; {name} stores them in SQLite on your server or computer, and its model judges, action by action,
whether a human or an AI agent was acting, which agent it was, and the human/agent share of each session.
After install you open a local page (http://127.0.0.1:{port}/): register, then it shows how to connect your
website (one line in its pages; for a public website, {name} on a server it can reach). Python {python} or newer,
standard library only.
Install dir:  $CAKE_HOME (default ~/.cake): config.json, cake.db (SQLite), replays/ (compressed replay chunks),
cake.pid, cake.log. `{command} migrate` copies a 0.3.4 database's replays into chunks (after a backup).
Port:         $CAKE_PORT or config "port" (default {port}). The local page listens on 127.0.0.1 only, always.
Settings:     {command} config get lists every setting, its value and where it comes from (default, user, env).
Use server mode to record visitors to a public website, with {name} on a small server that you own.
You can use Caddy to serve {name} on a subdomain of your site, such as https://cake.example.com/cake/. You can also
use your load balancer to send requests for a path of your site to {name}, such as https://example.com/cake/.
Server mode adds a second listener at the `public_listen` address. When Caddy runs in front of {name}, you can use
This listener serves only the page script, the rrweb recorder, the collect endpoint, and a health check. Use
`path_prefix` to set their path, such as /cake.
The dashboard, replay, and settings are available only on the local page at 127.0.0.1. To open the local page, use
an SSH tunnel.
When `trust_lb` is on, {name} reads the visitor's IP address, TLS fingerprint, and protocol from headers. Caddy or
your load balancer sets these headers: {lb_headers}.
{name} checks the IP address against published IP ranges. The ranges are in agentcake/data/lists/.
{name} also uses the IP address to look up the visitor's country, region, and city in the city database. {name}
never stores the IP address.
Your site's server can also send {name} details of each page request that only the server sees. The server sends
these details as a signed token in the `cake` entry of the Server-Timing header. The cake.js page script forwards
the token to {name}.
To create the shared secret, run `{command} secret init`. {name} stores the secret in $CAKE_HOME/srv_secret and uses
it to verify the token.
Keeping data: every session is recorded and kept; nothing is deleted by age unless you choose 30 or 90 days.
The database has a disk budget (`budget_mb`, default {budget_mb}). From {warn_pct}% the dashboard and settings warn,
with how long until full at last week's pace. When less than {free_left_pct}% of the budget is left and `auto_free` is
on (default), {name} deletes session REPLAYS (rrweb events), oldest first, across all session types, keeping
each session's classification, shares, timeline and server middleware data. With `auto_free` off, a full budget
stops new replays. When the disk itself has less than `disk_min_free_mb` free (default {disk_min_free_mb} MB),
{name} stops storing new replays and deletes none; they start again on their own once there is room. Each visit
and its classification are still recorded either way.
Commands: start | stop | status | serve (foreground, for systemd) | setup --print | setup --print --site [--dir DIR]
config get [key] | config set <key> <value> | snippet | doctor [--dir DIR] [--url URL] | ping | sentence
--version
secret init | secret print (the server middleware secret, for the site's server; printed only when asked)
lists (age and sources of the name and IP lists in use) | lists update (downloads the latest lists now)
migrate [--dry-run] (0.3.4 replays into compressed chunks; backs the database up first)
logs import <file>... [--since 10m] [--to URL] (page requests from an nginx, Apache or Caddy access log)
logs formats (the log formats it reads, and the recommended lines for each web server)
delete --session <id> | --visitor <visit id> [--dry-run] (every trace of a visit: database, replays,
backups/, cake.log; works while {name} runs)
eval [--gate] [--out DIR] (how well it judges sessions with known answers, against eval/thresholds.json)
lists_not_updated: lists not updated, the ones in use stay: {error}
places_not_updated: Unable to update the city database: {error}. {name} continues to use the current city database.

eval_options.about: Measures how well {name} judges sessions with known answers and checks the thresholds in eval/thresholds.json. It uses lab sessions, clean human recordings, splices and a CAKE_HOME's labelled sessions, with PostHog replays as reference only and a website's own labelled sessions held out. Reads only.
eval_options.gate: exit 0 only when every threshold this command measures passes (1 when one fails or has no data)
eval_options.out: folder to write eval.md and eval.json into
eval_options.no_logistic: skip training the lab's logistic regression on its splices (it takes minutes)
eval_options.sources: JSON file naming this computer's data folders (default: eval/sources.json of a checkout)
eval_options.cake_home: the CAKE_HOME whose sessions eval/truth_goal.jsonl lists (default: the current one)
eval_options.truth_goal: the list of labelled CAKE_HOME sessions (default: eval/truth_goal.jsonl)
eval_options.truth_manual: the list of clean human recordings
eval_options.truth_recordings: the list of agent and hand-off recordings
eval_options.thresholds: the thresholds file (default: eval/thresholds.json of a checkout)
eval_options.named_user_agents: named User-Agents for threshold A7 (default: eval/named_user_agents.json)
eval_options.selfcollect: the data folder of the recorder copy our own runs used (Claude Code with an MCP server, automation dressed up as a human)
eval_options.truth_selfcollect: the list of our own runs' recordings
eval_options.site_home: a copy of a website's data folder whose sessions --truth-site lists (held out: reported on its own)
eval_options.truth_site: the list of that website's labelled sessions

eval_no_thresholds: No thresholds file: {command} eval reads eval/thresholds.json and its data sets from a checkout of {name}'s source, which a release does not carry. Run the checkout's bin/{command} eval, or give --thresholds and the data sets (see {command} eval --help).
eval_from_checkout: {command} eval reads eval/thresholds.json and its data sets from a checkout of {name}'s source, which a release does not carry. Run the checkout's bin/{command} eval.
eval_gate_pass: Gate: every threshold measured here passes.
eval_gate_fail: Gate: not passing (failed or no data): {ids}.
logs_imported: {file} ({format}): {lines} lines; {sent} page requests sent: {matched} matched a visit, {duplicates} were already imported, {unmatched} matched no visit and were dropped; {skipped} other lines skipped, {older} older than --since, {unreadable} unreadable.
logs_missing: Not in this log format: {fields}. `{command} logs formats` prints the recommended format for nginx, Apache and Caddy.
logs_empty: Empty on every page request of this log: {fields}. Something in front of the web server (a proxy or a CDN) may remove them.
logs_no_format: {file}: no line of it is in a format {name} knows; give yours with --nginx-format or --apache-format.
logs_format_lacks: the log format has no {fields}; {name} needs each line's time, address, request, status and User-Agent
logs_bad_since: --since takes a number and a unit, s, m, h or d: for example --since 10m
logs_no_secret: no server middleware secret in {path}: on the {name} server `{command} secret print` prints it; put it there through a pipe (SERVER.md, "Server logs": {source}/SERVER.md)
logs_refused_secret: {url} answered {status}: the server middleware secret in {path} is not the one of that {name}
logs_refused: {url} answered {status}: the records were not taken
logs_unreachable: nothing answers at {url}: is {name} running there? ({error})
delete_usage: usage: {command} delete --session <id> | --visitor <visit id> (each as often as needed) [--dry-run]
delete_bad_id: not a session id: "{id}" ({name}'s ids are letters and digits, at most {max} of them); nothing was deleted
delete_unsure_running: {pid_file} names process {pid}, which is running, but no {name} answers on port {port}, so nothing was deleted. If {name} runs on another port, run this again with CAKE_PORT set to it; if process {pid} is not {name}, delete {pid_file}.
delete_done: deleted {id}: {rows} rows, and {chunks} replay chunks ({bytes:,} bytes) overwritten with zeros
delete_would: would delete {id}: {rows} rows and {chunks} replay chunks ({bytes:,} bytes)
delete_backups: deleted {rows} rows from {files} backup(s) in backups/
delete_backups_would: would delete {rows} rows from {files} backup(s) in backups/
delete_log_would: would remove {lines} lines naming it from {log}
delete_reclaim: replay space given back: {deleted} chunk files deleted, {compacted} compacted, {bytes:,} bytes
delete_not_rewritten: {file} could not be rewritten ({error}): what was deleted may leave traces in its free space until it is. Free some disk space and run the same command again.
delete_wal_busy: a reader still had the write-ahead log of {file} open, so it still holds old pages; run the same command again to empty it.
delete_api_bad_body: To delete specific sessions, send {{"sessions": ["<session id>", ...]}}. Session IDs can contain only letters and digits. To delete every session, send {{"all": true}}.
secret_created: secret created: {path} (mode 600, not printed). Give the same value to your site's server with: {command} secret print
invalid_choice: {key} must be one of the following values: {choices}.

invalid_setting.retention_days: Set retention_days to 0 to keep every session. Choose 30 or 90 to delete sessions older than that number of days.
invalid_setting.path_prefix: Enter a path for path_prefix, for example /cake. Use only letters, digits, dots, dashes, and slashes.
invalid_setting.public_listen: Enter host:port for public_listen, for example 0.0.0.0:8080. An empty value turns off server mode.
invalid_setting.public_url: Enter http:// or https:// and a host name for public_url, such as https://cake.example.com. Don't include a path or trailing slash, and enter the path in path_prefix. An empty value uses your site's own path.
invalid_setting.site_key: Start site_key with ck_, followed by 3 to 40 letters, digits, or underscores.
invalid_setting.site_domain: Enter a domain name for site_domain, such as shop.example.com, with or without a port.
invalid_setting.hide_selectors: For hide_selectors, enter up to 1,000 characters on one line. Don't include { or }.
invalid_setting.timezone: Enter an IANA time zone name for timezone, such as America/Los_Angeles or UTC. An empty value follows this computer's time zone.
invalid_setting.mask_inputs: The page script always masks visitor input. The mask_inputs setting is no longer available. For more information, see agentcake/data/privacy.json.

python_too_old: {name} needs Python {python} or newer, and this is Python {version} ({executable}). Install a newer Python 3 (3.14 or newer also keeps replays smaller) and run {command} with it.
did_not_stop: {name} (pid {pid}) was asked to stop but has not exited after {seconds} s; see {log}. Run  {launcher} stop  again to wait longer.
stop_not_allowed: {name} (pid {pid}) could not be stopped from here: {error}. It may run as another user, or a sandbox (an AI tool's) may not allow it; run  {launcher} stop  in your own terminal.
stop_pid_unreadable: {name} was not stopped: {file} holds no process id: {error}
public_listening: {name} public listener on {listen} prefix={prefix} trust_lb={trust_lb} server middleware={half} ranges={ranges}
ping_sent: Self-check visit sent (page script HTTP {status}); it is marked as a test.
ping_failed: Could not send the self-check visit: {error}
doctor_replays_zlib: (Python {version} has no compression.zstd, so replays are stored with zlib and take more disk; Python 3.14+ uses zstd)
doctor_replays_unreadable: {count} stored chunks are zstd and need Python 3.14+ to be read
doctor_replays_blocked: not checked: writing in {folder} is not allowed from here ({error}), though its permissions allow it: most likely a sandbox (an AI tool's) blocks writing outside its own folder, not a problem with {name}'s storage. Ask the user to run  {launcher} doctor  in their own terminal to check it
doctor_site_none: Your own website (optional): not connected. Fine; connect it only if the user asks (setup --print --site).
doctor_logs_info: {format}, last import {when}: {records} page requests, {matched} matched a visit
doctor_logs_no_address: ; no line can match: the uploads carry no visitor address (turn on trust_lb behind your load balancer, SERVER.md: {source}/SERVER.md)
doctor_logs_formats: (`{command} logs formats` prints the recommended format)
doctor_sandbox_note: Note: if '{command} start' fails with 'Operation not permitted', a sandbox is blocking local network access, not {name}.
doctor_blocked: no connection to {base} is allowed from here ({error}): a sandbox (an AI tool's) blocks local network access, so this cannot tell whether {name} runs; it may well be running
doctor_blocked_next: {name} itself may be fine. Do not start it again: ask the user to run  {launcher} doctor  in their own terminal, or to give this tool network access (Codex: -c sandbox_workspace_write.network_access=true).
doctor_not_checked_blocked: not checked: the sandbox blocks connections to 127.0.0.1
doctor_not_health: something answers on {base}, but not {name}'s health check (HTTP {status})
doctor_all_passed_warn: All checks passed, with {count} warning(s) above. Open {base}/
doctor_python_no_zstd: compression.zstd: no (replays are stored with zlib and take about 1.4 times the disk; Python 3.14+ has zstd)
doctor_disk_ok: {free} MB free on the disk of {folder}; below {floor} MB (disk_min_free_mb) {below}
doctor_disk_off_info: {free} MB free on the disk of {folder}; {off}
doctor_disk_low: only {free} MB free on the disk of {folder}, below the {floor} MB set in disk_min_free_mb, so {replays_stop}; {resume}. Visits and classifications are still recorded. {name} deletes no replays to make room. {fix}
doctor_disk_replays_resume: they start again automatically once there is room
doctor_disk_fix: Free some space, or lower the floor:  {launcher} config set disk_min_free_mb <MB>
doctor_lists_info: built {built}, {age} day(s) old ({location}; over {max_age} days old asks for an update)
doctor_lists_stale: built {built}, {age} days old, over {max_age}: run  {launcher} lists update  (it goes online to fetch them) or upgrade {name}
doctor_places_info: The city database is DB-IP IP to City Lite for {month}, stored in {folder}.
doctor_places_missing: Until the city database is downloaded, the country of every visitor is Not set.
doctor_places_command: To download the database over the internet, run this command:  {launcher} lists update
doctor_places_first_update: {name} downloads the database at its first automatic update, {first} to {last} minutes after it starts.
doctor_places_stale: This city database is from {month} and is now {months} months old. To download the latest version over the internet, run this command:  {launcher} lists update
doctor_places_unreadable: {name} can't read the city database because of this error: {error}. To download it again, run this command:  {launcher} lists update
doctor_updates_on: Automatic updates are on. {name} downloads the latest lists every {days} days.
doctor_updates_on_server: Automatic updates are on. {name} downloads the latest lists and city database every {days} days.
doctor_updates_last_ok: The last update ran at {when} and succeeded.
doctor_updates_last_failed: The last update failed at {when} with this error: {error}
doctor_updates_retry: {name} tries the update again the next day.
doctor_updates_failing: The last {count} updates failed. The most recent error was: {error}
doctor_updates_command: To update now, run this command:  {launcher} lists update
doctor_path_none: not on PATH: run it as  {launcher}
doctor_path_other: {command} runs {path}, which is not this installation ({launcher}): run this one by its full path, or remove the other one
doctor_site_middleware: Server middleware in the site's code
doctor_site_middleware_none: no file mounts {middleware}: setup --print --site says where it goes
doctor_site_middleware_beside: {files} missing beside the middleware's other files: copy it from {name}'s edge folder (setup --print --site)
doctor_site_middleware_folder: The {folder} folder is missing from the site's code. To find out how to add it, run this command:  {launcher} setup --print --site
doctor_site_middleware_unlisted: The dependencies in package.json don't include {package}. To add it, install the {folder} folder with the site's package manager. With npm, run this command:  npm install --save-prod ./{folder}
doctor_site_middleware_package: The dependencies in package.json install {package} from {spec}. To install it from the {folder} folder instead, use the site's package manager. With npm, run this command:  npm install ./{folder}
doctor_site_middleware_static: not needed: a static site has no server code (the server middleware is optional)
doctor_site_middleware_unknown: not checked: the framework was not recognised
doctor_site_script_plugin: not in the files: the {name} plugin adds the line (a page opened with site_url shows it)
doctor_site_plugin_found: {files} (activate it under Plugins, and fill in Settings > {name})
doctor_site_plugin_none: the {name} plugin is not in wp-content/plugins: setup --print --site says how to add it
doctor_site_plugin_elsewhere: Theme and plugin folders don't include the {name} plugin, which is installed on the WordPress site. To check the plugin, set site_url to a page on that site.
doctor_live_script_none: no cake.js line with this site key in the page
doctor_live_blocked: a sandbox (an AI tool's) blocks connections from here: run doctor in your own terminal, or allow network access
doctor_live_cert_dates: A certificate in the HTTPS chain of {host} is outside its validity period. Doctor compares this period with the date and time on this computer. If the date and time are correct, replace the certificate.
doctor_live_cert_self_signed: The HTTPS certificate for {host} is self-signed. Python doesn't trust self-signed certificates by default. For a public website, get a certificate from a certificate authority, such as Let's Encrypt. For a development server, run doctor with an http:// address, or add the server's certificate to the certificates that Python trusts.
doctor_live_cert_name: The HTTPS certificate from {host} doesn't match the host name {host}. Make sure that the DNS record for {host} points to the site's server. Then make sure that the server uses a certificate for {host}. On many hosting platforms, you get this certificate when you add {host} to the site's domains.
doctor_live_cert_ip: The HTTPS certificate from {host} isn't valid for this IP address. Run doctor again with an address that uses the site's domain name. If the site has no domain name, the server needs a certificate issued for this IP address.
doctor_live_cert_issuer: The HTTPS certificate chain for {host} doesn't end at a certificate authority that Python trusts. Make sure that the server at {host} sends all intermediate certificates. A proxy on this network that replaces certificates can also cause this error. A missing root certificate in Python's trust store can also cause this error.
doctor_live_cert_strict: A certificate in the HTTPS chain of {host} fails a strict check in Python 3.13 and later. Python reports this error: {reason}. Replace the failing certificate. A proxy on this network that replaces certificates can also cause this error.
doctor_live_cert_other: Doctor can't verify the HTTPS certificate for {host}. Python reports this error: {reason}.
doctor_live_token_ok: Server-Timing cake, signed with this {name}'s secret, {age} s old
doctor_live_token_none: no cake entry in the response's Server-Timing: the middleware is not mounted, or the site's server has no {env}
doctor_live_token_cached: A page cache{seen} served this page without a token. At an uncached address, your site's server returns a valid token. To give every page view a token, turn on {option}. If you keep the cache, {name} still records views of cached pages. These views don't have server middleware data.
doctor_live_token_cache_timeout: The page has no token{seen}. A page cache sends stored pages without a token. Doctor can't check the server middleware, because an uncached copy of the page didn't arrive within {seconds} seconds. To try again, run doctor. If requests need more time, run this command:  {launcher} config set http_timeout_s <seconds>
doctor_live_token_bad: signed with another secret: the site's server needs this {name}'s, the value of  {launcher} secret print
doctor_live_token_stale: its time is {minutes} min away from the clock of the machine {name} runs on, outside the window a token counts in: check both clocks
doctor_live_no_secret: this {name} has no secret yet, so it cannot read a token: run  {launcher} secret init  and give the site's server the value of  {launcher} secret print
doctor_live_token_optional: The page has no token because this site doesn't use the server middleware. The middleware is optional for a static site.
doctor_live_sec_fetch: Doctor's Sec-Fetch values in the token
doctor_live_signature: Signature headers at the site's server
doctor_live_lost: {headers} did not reach the site's server: something in front of it (a proxy, a CDN, a load balancer) removes them
doctor_live_not_checked: not checked: no token to read
doctor_live_no_url: not checked: save a page of the running site with  {launcher} config set site_url <address>  (or run doctor --url <address>)
doctor_public_header_path: Server mode on a path of your site ({url}):
doctor_public_no_site_domain: This check is skipped until site_domain is set. The self-check needs your website's domain. To set the domain, run this command:  {launcher} config set site_domain <your domain>
doctor_public_dns_none: No DNS record exists for {host} yet. The lookup fails with this message: {error}. Add an A record for {host} with this server's public IPv4 address, and an AAAA record if the server has IPv6. Add the records at your DNS provider. They take effect within a few minutes to a few hours.
doctor_public_dns_cdn: {host} points to {address}, an address that belongs to {cdn}. Browsers connect to {cdn} first. {name} then receives visitor IP addresses only if Caddy reads them from a {cdn} header. The checks below show whether Caddy reads the header. {fix}
doctor_public_cert_info: The certificate for {host} is valid until {until}.
doctor_public_cert_no_connection: The connection to {host} fails with this error: {error}. {hint}
doctor_public_cert_hint: Caddy obtains its certificate from Let's Encrypt automatically. To do this, the DNS record for {host} must point to this server, and ports 80 and 443 must be open to the internet. If the DNS record and ports are correct, check Caddy's log for errors.
doctor_public_cert_http: {url} doesn't use HTTPS. On pages served over HTTPS, browsers block cake.js from this address as mixed content. Set public_url to https://{host}.
doctor_public_this_info: The response from {url} includes this server's site key.
doctor_public_this_other: The response from {url} has HTTP status {status} and doesn't include this server's site key. This means that the address leads to a different server. Point the DNS record for {host} to this server. Make sure that Caddy forwards {prefix}/cake.js and {prefix}/collect to {name}.
doctor_public_this_upstream: HTTP {status} from {url} means that the server for {host} can't reach the public listener of {name}. In the Caddyfile, make sure that reverse_proxy sends requests to {listen}. This is the address in the public_listen setting.
doctor_public_cors_info: The OPTIONS request returns HTTP 204. {name} allows requests from {origin}.
doctor_public_cors_bad: {problems} As a result, browsers on {origin} can't read the responses. Whenever a response can't be read, cake.js retries the upload. {name} sends CORS headers from version 0.6.0. If your version is older, upgrade {name}. Otherwise, a proxy, CDN, or other server in front of {name} blocks OPTIONS or removes Access-Control-Allow-Origin.
doctor_public_cors_options: The OPTIONS request returns HTTP {status}. The response has Access-Control-Allow-Origin set to {allow}.
doctor_public_cors_upload: The upload response has Access-Control-Allow-Origin set to {allow}.
doctor_public_upload_info: Doctor sends a test upload to {url} with the Origin header {origin}. The upload arrives{through} with its Accept-Language, User-Agent, and Host headers unchanged.
doctor_public_upload_status: Doctor sends a test upload to {url}{through}. The response has HTTP status {status}. {name} doesn't receive the upload. {fix}
doctor_public_upload_failed: Doctor can't reach {url}. The connection fails with this error: {error}.
doctor_public_upload_lost: Doctor sends a test upload to {url}{through}. The response has HTTP status {status}. However, {name} on this server doesn't receive the upload. This means that the address leads to a different server.
doctor_public_upload_changed: The test upload reaches {name}{through} with changed headers. {changes} {fix}
doctor_public_upload_retried: Doctor sends a test upload to {url}{through}. The upload reaches {name} on this server. The response has HTTP status {status}. For cake.js, this status means that the upload failed. As a result, every upload is sent again.
doctor_public_made_up: Doctor sends {header} with test data. {name} accepts this test data as the visitor's {header} value. This means that visitors can set this header themselves. {fix}
doctor_public_made_up_fix: In the Caddyfile, add the line  header_up -{header}  to reverse_proxy so that visitors can't set this header.
doctor_public_made_up_fix_path: Make sure that the load balancer overwrites or clears {header} on every request. For details, see {source}/SERVER.md.
doctor_public_address_info: {kind}. Doctor sent the self-check from this server. The address doesn't belong to a CDN.
doctor_public_address_unlisted: An IP address that isn't in any listed network
doctor_public_address_cdn: {name} receives an IP address from {cdn} instead of the visitor's IP address. With this setup, every visitor would get the {cdn} address, and crawler IP address checks would give incorrect results. {fix}
doctor_public_address_none: {name} receives the self-check without a visitor IP address. Without this address, {name} can't verify crawler IP addresses. {fix}
doctor_public_address_none_fix: In the Caddyfile, add  header_up X-Cake-Client-IP {{client_ip}}  to reverse_proxy.
doctor_public_address_none_fix_path: Make sure that the load balancer writes the visitor's IP address to X-Cake-Client-IP. For details, see {source}/SERVER.md.
doctor_public_address_off: The trust_lb setting is off. {name} doesn't read visitor IP addresses or check crawler IP addresses. If Caddy is in front of {name}, run this command to turn on trust_lb:  {launcher} config set trust_lb true
doctor_public_address_off_path: This check is skipped because the trust_lb setting is off. {name} reads visitor IP addresses only when this setting is on. For details, see {source}/SERVER.md.
doctor_public_visitors_info: In {cdn} of {sessions} recent sessions, the IP address belongs to a CDN.
doctor_public_visitors_none: No recent sessions have an IP address yet.
doctor_public_visitors_cdn: In {cdn} of {sessions} recent sessions, the IP address belongs to a CDN. {name} receives the CDN's address instead of each visitor's address. As a result, {name} marks crawler names as self-reported. The dashboard also shows a warning. {fix}
doctor_public_visitors_unknown: An earlier version of {name} is running. Only newer versions report the data for this check.
doctor_public_why_dns: The public address has no DNS record yet. This check can run only after you add the record.
doctor_public_why_https: Doctor can't connect to the public address. This check runs only when doctor can connect.
doctor_public_why_other: Requests to {url} don't reach {name} on this server. Doctor can't test {name} through that address.
doctor_public_why_local: {name} on this computer isn't responding. Doctor registers each self-check with {name} on this computer before sending it. As a result, a self-check never counts as a visit.
doctor_public_why_upload: The self-check upload didn't reach {name}. There's no IP address to check.
doctor_public_why_down: There's no response from {name}, so this check was skipped.
doctor_public_fix_headers: Forward {prefix}/ with the browser's original headers. In CloudFront, use the AllViewer origin request policy. In Apache, add  ProxyPreserveHost On  to the configuration. In nginx, add  proxy_set_header Host $host;  to the location that forwards {prefix}/.
doctor_public_fix_address: Point the DNS record for {host} directly to this server. Make sure that no proxy is in front of Caddy.
doctor_public_fix_address_path: Make sure that the load balancer writes the visitor's IP address to X-Cake-Client-IP. As an alternative, set proxy_hops to the number of proxies in front of {name}. For details, see {source}/SERVER.md.
doctor_public_fix_forward: Make sure that the server for {host} forwards {prefix}/collect to {name}.
doctor_public_fix_cloudfront_methods: In CloudFront, make sure that the {prefix}/* behavior forwards requests to {name}. For Allowed HTTP methods, choose GET, HEAD, OPTIONS, PUT, POST, PATCH, DELETE.
doctor_public_fix_cloudfront: CloudFront: Use the AllViewer origin request policy for the {prefix}/* behavior. This policy forwards the browser's Accept-Language, User-Agent, and Host headers.
doctor_public_fix_cloudflare: Cloudflare: The Worker that forwards {prefix}/ must pass on the request's headers unchanged. For example, the Worker can call fetch(url, request). You can also set up a DNS-only subdomain for {name}, as described in {source}/SERVER.md.
doctor_public_fix_cloudflare_address: Cloudflare: Make sure that the Worker that forwards {prefix}/ sets X-Cake-Client-IP to the request's CF-Connecting-IP. As an alternative, set proxy_hops to 1.
doctor_public_fix_cloudflare_dns: In Cloudflare's DNS settings, set the record for {host} to DNS only (gray cloud) so that browsers connect to this server directly. You can also keep the proxy and run Caddy with the deploy/Caddyfile configuration. This configuration reads each visitor's IP address from CF-Connecting-IP when a request comes from Cloudflare's IP ranges.
doctor_public_fix_vercel: Vercel: A rewrite to another server replaces the browser's Host header. Vercel has no option to keep the original header. Instead, set up a subdomain for {name}, such as cake.<your domain>, as described in {source}/SERVER.md.
doctor_public_fix_azure: Azure Front Door: Leave the origin host header empty so that the browser's Host header is kept.
doctor_public_fix_nginx: nginx: Add  proxy_set_header Host $host;  to the location that forwards {prefix}/. By default, nginx sends the upstream's name as the Host header.
doctor_public_fix_apache: Apache: Add  ProxyPreserveHost On  next to the ProxyPass for {prefix}/. By default, Apache sends the backend's name as the Host header.
doctor_public_fix_caddy: Caddy: In the Caddyfile, add  header_up Host {{host}}  to reverse_proxy. Caddy replaces the Host header when the upstream uses HTTPS.
